subject_hint: Art Blakey and the Afro-Drum Ensemble — The African Beat (recorded 1962) — On the anniversary of Blakey's death, a less-played corner of his catalogue: a Blue Note date built around Nigerian singer and talking-drum player Solomon Ilori, who wrote four of its seven pieces. Notes: Death date and place (lung cancer, St. Vincent's, Manhattan) on both pages; 36th anniversary, not a round number: write 'died on this day in 1990', no anniversary count needed. Album facts, personnel and composers from the album page: Ilori composed 'Prayer', 'Ife L'ayo', 'Ero Ti Nr'Ojeje', 'Ayiko, Ayiko'; 'Love, The Mystery of' is by Guy Warren (Guy Warren is in the log 2026-10-12, expired: mention only as composer credit, not as the subject). Blakey's West African stay (1948-49 per Wikipedia; 'nearly two years' per EBSCO; Blakey himself quoted as saying about two years) and his discouraging comparisons with African drumming: both pages; attribute and avoid a firm duration. Ilori's own biography (birthplace, later life) not yet sourced: find a page before stating it. Nat Hentoff wrote the liner notes. Slot 3 is also jazz under the rotation: choosing #1 with #5 or #6 gives two jazz posts on the day. RESEARCH (2026-10-15): see sources.md. Do NOT say Ilori wrote four of seven pieces (single source); say the album opens with Ilori's Prayer / Ilori credited with several pieces. No Ilori biography beyond Nigerian singer and percussionist. Blakey West Africa: "after his 1948 trip", no duration.
artist: Art Blakey (drums, timpani, telegraph drum, gong) and the Afro-Drum Ensemble: Solomon G. Ilori (vocals, talking drum, pennywhistle), Yusef Lateef (tenor saxophone, flute, oboe, cow horn, mbira), Ahmed Abdul-Malik (bass), Chief Bey, Montego Joe, Robert Crowder, James Ola Folami, Garvin Masseaux (percussion), Curtis Fuller (timpani)
work: The African Beat (Blue Note BLP 4097; recorded January 24, 1962, Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs; released November 1962; produced by Alfred Lion; engineer Rudy Van Gelder)
calendar: Art Blakey died at St. Vincent's Hospital in Manhattan, New York, on October 16, 1990.
